observations: Photo 0 shows a used car engine on a workshop floor, turbocharger and intercooler piping visible, wiring harness and sensors attached.
No engine code, casting number, or manufacturer plate is legible anywhere in the photo.
Watermark reads 'CAMON 40' (phone camera brand), not related to the engine.
No vehicle, VIN, or fitment label visible to confirm which car model this engine belongs to.
No video or sound clip showing the engine running is provided despite the 'tested and working' claim.

claims.evidence: No paperwork, import sticker, or guarantee document shown in photo 0.
Contradicts the same seller's claim of 'Direct Japan' in the same message; origin cannot both be Japan and Belgium.
No start-up video, compression test, or sound clip provided; photo shows a static, disconnected engine.
Cannot be assessed from a still photo; requires audio/video of running engine.
No odometer, service sticker, or mileage document visible; engines alone carry no mileage proof.
No sign of factory seals, untouched bolt paint, or sealed gasket shown in photo.

risks.risk: Engine model/fitment unknown, which drives price enormously (from basic 4-cylinder petrol to premium diesel/V-engine).
risks.proof: Clear close-up of the engine code/casting number stamped on the block, or a VIN/parts tag.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all, since worst-case range spans the entire comparable list

risks.risk: Internal condition (compression, knocking, oil sludge) cannot be seen in a static photo.
risks.proof: Video of the engine running/idling with audible sound, plus a compression test printout.

risks.risk: Origin claim is self-contradictory (Japan vs Belgium), raising doubt about the whole history and documentation.
risks.proof: Import/customs paperwork or auction sheet showing country of origin and mileage.
risks.if_unproven: treated as unverifiable origin, no premium for 'low mileage' or 'direct import' claims

risks.risk: Turbocharger and sensor wiring condition unknown; turbo failure is costly and common in used Tokunbo engines.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of turbo shaft play and intact wiring/connectors.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if turbo needs replacement

proof_requests: Photo of the engine code/casting number stamped on the block (e.g., near the cylinder head or block face).
A video of the engine starting and idling with audible sound, to check for knocking.
Any import/customs document or auction sheet showing mileage and country of origin.
Close-up of the turbocharger and wiring harness for visible wear or damage.
Clarification from the seller on the real country of origin (Japan or Belgium).
response.reason: The engine's make/model cannot be read from the single photo, and comparable prices vary by over 6x depending on engine type, so no worst-case price can be set without a legible engine code or fitment proof; the seller's origin claim is also internally contradictory.
